lessons.title: My family
lessons.canDo: Name the people in your family
lessons.scenario: Smarty visits Mia in the living room and meets her mother, father, brother, and sister.

items.note: Say 'mother' for your female parent.

image.describe: a warm, smiling adult female cat standing in a cozy living room

items.note: Say 'father' for your male parent.

image.describe: a friendly adult male cat wearing glasses and smiling warmly

items.note: Say 'brother' for a boy or man with the same parents as you.

image.describe: a cheerful young male cat waving hello

items.note: Say 'sister' for a girl or woman with the same parents as you.

image.describe: a happy young female cat smiling brightly

items.note: Put 'my' before a person or thing to show it belongs to you.

grammar.title: Using 'my' to introduce people
grammar.explanation: Put 'my' before a family word to show they belong to you, such as 'my mother' or 'my brother'.

practice.prompt: Look at the picture of a female parent. Which word matches?
practice.explanation: Mother is the word for a female parent.

practice.prompt: Look at the picture of a male parent. Which word matches?
practice.explanation: Father is the word for a male parent.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.explanation: Sam is a boy, so he is a brother.

practice.prompt: Match each sentence with the person it describes.
practice.explanation: Mother and sister are female; father and brother are male.

practice.prompt: Complete the sentence to introduce your sister.
practice.explanation: Use 'my' before 'sister' to show she is your sister.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence to introduce your mother.
practice.explanation: Start with 'This is', then add 'my mother'.

practice.prompt: Ben is a boy in your home. Complete the sentence.
practice.explanation: Ben is male, so the right word is 'brother'.

practice.prompt: Say this sentence aloud.
practice.explanation: Use 'my sister' to introduce a female sibling.

story.hook: Who does Smarty meet in Mia's living room?

image.describe: Mia's cozy living room: Smarty the black cat shakes paws with Mia's mother, father, brother Sam, and sister Ana.

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: Good morning, Mia!

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: Hello, Smarty! This is my mother.

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: Nice to meet you!

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: This is my father, and this is my brother Sam.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: Hi, Smarty! Ana is my sister.

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: Hello, Smarty! I am happy to meet you.

questions.explanation: Mia says: This is my brother Sam.
Sam says: Ana is my sister.
Mia says first: This is my mother.

mission.setup: Smarty wants to meet the people in your home. Introduce someone using 'my'.

turns.smarty: Hello! This is my mother. And you?
turns.hint: Say 'This is my mother' or 'This is my father'.

turns.smarty: Nice! Do you say brother or sister for a girl?
turns.hint: Say 'sister'.

lessons.title: This is my
lessons.scenario: Mia and Sam show Smarty their parents and baby sister Lily in the living room.

items.note: Say 'baby' for a very small child; more than one is 'babies'.

image.describe: a tiny baby kitten smiling inside a soft cozy basket

items.note: Say 'parents' when you talk about a mother and father together.

image.describe: a mother cat and a father cat standing side by side and smiling

items.note: Use 'his' when something belongs to a boy or man.
Use 'her' when something belongs to a girl or woman.
Use 'our' when something belongs to you and another person together.

grammar.title: my, his, her, our
grammar.explanation: Match the word to the owner: 'my' is for me, 'his' is for a boy or man, 'her' is for a girl or woman, and 'our' is for me and someone else together.

practice.prompt: Look at the picture of a very small child. Which word fits?
practice.explanation: A very small child is a baby.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.explanation: Parents means mother and father together.

practice.prompt: Sam is a boy. Complete the sentence about his mother.
practice.explanation: Use 'his' for a boy: his mother.

practice.prompt: Mia is a girl. Complete the sentence about her father.
practice.explanation: Use 'her' for a girl: her father.

practice.prompt: You and Sam share the same baby sister. Build the sentence.
practice.explanation: Use 'our' when something belongs to both of you.

practice.prompt: Match each word with who it is for.
practice.explanation: My is for me, his is for a boy, her is for a girl, and our is for us.

practice.prompt: Mia and Sam talk about their mother and father together. Complete the sentence.
practice.explanation: Use 'parents' for a mother and father together.

practice.prompt: Say this sentence aloud.
practice.explanation: Lily is a girl, so we say 'Her name is Lily.'

story.hook: Who is sleeping in the basket in Mia and Sam's living room?

image.describe: Mia and Sam stand beside their mother and father in the living room while a tiny baby kitten Lily smiles in a basket.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: Smarty, this is our mother and this is our father.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: Yes, our parents are here.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: And this is our baby sister.

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: What is her name?

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: Her name is Lily.

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: Hello, Lily! She is a happy baby.

questions.prompt: Who are Mia and Sam's mother and father together?
questions.explanation: Sam says: Yes, our parents are here.
Sam says: Her name is Lily.

questions.prompt: Mia says: This is ___ baby sister.
questions.explanation: Mia and Sam share the baby sister, so Mia says 'our'.

mission.setup: Smarty asks you about Mia, Sam, and their baby sister Lily.

turns.smarty: Sam has a sister. Is Mia his sister or her sister?
turns.hint: Sam is a boy, so say 'his sister'.

turns.smarty: Are your parents happy?
turns.hint: Say 'Yes, my parents are happy.'

lessons.title: Who is she?
lessons.scenario: Smarty looks at portraits on Ben's living room wall and asks about his grandmother and grandfather.

items.example: Who is she? She is my grandmother.
items.note: Ask 'Who is she?' when you want to know a girl or woman's name or role.
Say 'grandmother' for the mother of your mother or father.

image.describe: a kind older female cat with silver fur and a gentle smile

items.note: Say 'grandfather' for the father of your mother or father.

image.describe: a friendly older male cat with whiskers and round glasses

items.example: Who is it? It is Ben.
items.note: Use 'it' when you do not know who is there yet, or for a thing.

grammar.title: Asking 'Who is...?'
grammar.explanation: Use 'Who is she?' for a girl or woman, 'Who is he?' for a boy or man, and 'Who is it?' before you see who is there.
examples: Who is she? She is my grandmother.
Who is he? He is my grandfather.
Who is it? It is Smarty.

practice.prompt: Look at the picture of an older female relative. Which word matches?
practice.explanation: Grandmother is the mother of your mother or father.

practice.prompt: Look at the picture of an older male relative. Which word matches?
practice.explanation: Grandfather is the father of your mother or father.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.explanation: She is for a girl or woman: Who is she?

practice.prompt: Someone knocks. Complete the question and answer.
practice.explanation: Answer 'Who is it?' with 'It is...'.

practice.prompt: Ask who the woman in the picture is.
practice.explanation: Put 'Who', then 'is', then 'she'.

practice.prompt: Match each question with the right answer.
practice.explanation: Match 'she' with grandmother, 'he' with grandfather, and 'it' with It is.

practice.prompt: Say this sentence aloud.
practice.explanation: Use 'She is my grandmother' to introduce your grandmother.

story.hook: Who are the two older cats in Ben's living room?

image.describe: Ben's living room: Ben shows Smarty his smiling grandmother and grandfather sitting on a sofa.

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: Hello, Ben! Who is it?

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.text: It is my grandmother and my grandfather!

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: Who is she?

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.text: She is my grandmother. Her name is Zara.

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: Nice to meet you, Zara! And he is your grandfather?

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.text: Yes! He is my grandfather. His name is Omar.

questions.explanation: Ben says: She is my grandmother. Her name is Zara.
Ben says: He is my grandfather. His name is Omar.

questions.prompt: What question does Smarty ask about Zara?
questions.explanation: Smarty asks: Who is she?

mission.setup: Smarty points at a woman and a man in Ben's living room. Ask and answer who they are.

turns.smarty: I see a woman. Ask me who she is!
turns.hint: Ask 'Who is she?'

turns.smarty: She is Ben's grandmother! Now tell me about your grandfather.
turns.hint: Say 'He is my grandfather.' or 'This is my grandfather.'

lessons.title: Review
lessons.scenario: Leo and Zara introduce their parents, baby, grandmother, and grandfather to Smarty in the living room.

practice.prompt: Match each pair of family words.
practice.explanation: Each pair shows the female and male family members.

practice.prompt: Zara is a girl. Complete the sentence about her grandmother.
practice.explanation: Zara is a girl, so use 'her'.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.explanation: Our parents means the mother and father of both of us.

practice.prompt: Build the question to ask who a woman is.
practice.explanation: Use 'Who is she?' to ask about a female person.

practice.prompt: Leo has a very small brother. Complete the sentence.
practice.explanation: A very small brother is a baby brother.

practice.prompt: Someone is at the door. Complete: Who is ___?
practice.explanation: We ask 'Who is it?' before we know who is there.

practice.prompt: Say this sentence aloud.
practice.text: This is my grandfather and my grandmother.
practice.answer: This is my grandfather and my grandmother.
practice.explanation: Use 'my' before each family member you introduce.

story.hook: Who visits Zara's living room today?

image.describe: Zara's living room: Zara, Leo, their parents, baby brother Tom, and their grandmother greet Smarty.

lines.speaker: Zara
lines.text: Hello, Smarty! Leo is my brother.

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.text: This is our baby brother. His name is Tom.

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: Hello, baby Tom! Who is she?

lines.speaker: Zara
lines.text: She is our grandmother.

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.text: And our parents are happy to meet you!

questions.explanation: Leo says: This is our baby brother. His name is Tom.

questions.prompt: Who does Smarty ask about with 'Who is she?'
questions.explanation: Zara answers: She is our grandmother.

questions.prompt: How are Zara and Leo's parents?
questions.explanation: Leo says: And our parents are happy to meet you!

mission.setup: Tell Smarty about two people in your home using words from Lessons 1–3.

turns.smarty: Who is in your home? Introduce one person!
turns.hint: Say 'This is my mother' or 'She is my grandmother.'

turns.smarty: Wonderful! And how are your parents?
turns.hint: Say 'My parents are fine.' or 'My parents are happy.'

lessons.title: How old are you?
lessons.scenario: Smarty asks Mia, Sam, and Mia's sister how old they are in the living room.

items.example: Hello, Mia! How old are you?
items.note: Ask 'How old are you?' to find out someone's age.
Put 'years old' after a number to say someone's age.
Eleven is the number 11, right after ten.
Twelve is the number 12, right after eleven.

items.example: My sister is twenty years old.
items.note: Twenty is the number 20, two tens.

grammar.title: Saying ages in English
grammar.explanation: In English, use 'am', 'is', or 'are' with a number and 'years old'—for example, 'I am eleven years old' or 'She is twenty years old'.
examples: My sister is twenty years old.

practice.prompt: Match each number word with its digits.
practice.explanation: Eleven is 11, twelve is 12, and twenty is 20.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.explanation: 'How old are you?' asks about age.

practice.prompt: Complete the sentence to say Mia's age.
practice.explanation: Add 'years old' after the number.

practice.prompt: Sam is 12. Build the sentence about his age.
practice.explanation: Put the number 'twelve' before 'years old'.

practice.prompt: Ana is 20. Which word means 20?
practice.explanation: Twenty is 20.

practice.prompt: Say this question aloud.
practice.explanation: Use 'How old are you?' to ask someone's age.

story.hook: How old are Mia, Sam, and their sister Ana?

image.describe: Smarty chats with Mia, Sam, and older sister Ana in the living room while holding up number cards 11, 12, and 20.

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: Mia, how old are you?

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: I am eleven years old.

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: And Sam? How old is your brother?

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: I am twelve years old!

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: Our sister Ana is twenty years old.

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: Eleven, twelve, and twenty!

questions.explanation: Mia says: I am eleven years old.
Sam says: I am twelve years old!
Mia says: Our sister Ana is twenty years old.

mission.setup: Smarty wants to know your age! Any number from 1 to 20 works.

turns.smarty: Hello! How old are you?
turns.hint: Say 'I am eleven years old.' or 'I am twenty years old.'

turns.smarty: Now ask me my age!
turns.hint: Ask 'How old are you?'

lessons.title: My friends
lessons.canDo: Talk about friends in the plural
lessons.scenario: Omar introduces his best friends—boys and girls—to Smarty in the living room.

items.note: Say 'best friend' for your closest friend, and add -s for more than one: 'best friends'.

image.describe: two happy young cats hugging and smiling together as best friends

items.note: Say 'boy' for a male child, and 'boys' for more than one.

image.describe: a cheerful young male kitten wearing a blue scarf

items.note: Say 'girl' for a female child, and 'girls' for more than one.

image.describe: a cheerful young female kitten wearing a yellow ribbon

items.note: Use 'they' when you talk about two or more people or things.
Use 'they are' with plural nouns like 'friends', 'boys', or 'girls'.

grammar.title: Plurals and 'they are'
grammar.explanation: Add -s to talk about more than one person: boy → boys, girl → girls, friend → friends. Use 'they are' for two or more people.

practice.prompt: Look at the picture of a male child. Which word fits?
practice.explanation: A male child is a boy.

practice.prompt: Look at the picture of a female child. Which word fits?
practice.explanation: A female child is a girl.

practice.prompt: Match one person with two or more people.
practice.explanation: Add -s at the end to make these words plural.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.explanation: 'They are' is used for two or more people.

practice.prompt: Mia and Zara are two girls. Complete the sentence.
practice.explanation: Use 'They' for two girls together.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence about Leo and Sam.
practice.explanation: Use 'They are' and the plural 'boys' for two boys.

practice.prompt: Say this sentence aloud.
practice.explanation: Use 'my best friend' for your closest friend.

story.hook: Who are Omar's best friends in the living room?

image.describe: Omar stands in the living room with two boys, Leo and Ben, and two girls, Mia and Zara, smiling at Smarty.

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: Hello, Omar! Who are they?

lines.speaker: Omar
lines.text: They are my best friends!

lines.speaker: Omar
lines.text: Leo and Ben are boys. They are twelve years old.

lines.speaker: Omar
lines.text: Mia and Zara are girls. They are eleven years old.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: Yes! We are best friends, and we are happy!

questions.explanation: Omar says: Leo and Ben are boys.
Omar says: Mia and Zara are girls.
Omar talks about four friends, so he says 'They are'.

mission.setup: Tell Smarty about your best friend or your friends.

turns.smarty: Mia is my best friend! Who is your best friend?
turns.hint: Say a name + 'is my best friend', like 'Leo is my best friend.'

turns.smarty: Are your friends happy?
turns.hint: Say 'Yes, they are happy.'

lessons.title: Big and small
lessons.scenario: Smarty compares tall, short, big, small, and young family members in the living room.

items.note: Use 'big' for large size or an older brother or sister.

image.describe: a large, sturdy adult cat standing beside a tiny mouse toy

items.note: Use 'small' for little size, the opposite of 'big'.

image.describe: a tiny kitten sitting next to a big armchair

items.note: Use 'tall' when someone has great height.

image.describe: a very tall, lanky cat reaching near the top of a doorway

items.note: Use 'short' when someone is not tall.

image.describe: a little, low-to-the-ground kitten standing next to a tall cat

items.note: Use 'young' for someone who has lived only a few years, like a baby or child.

grammar.title: Adjective + noun
grammar.explanation: In English, describing words like 'big', 'small', 'tall', 'short', and 'young' go BEFORE the noun: 'a tall boy', 'a small baby'.

practice.prompt: Match each describing word with its opposite.
practice.explanation: Big is the opposite of small; tall is the opposite of short; young is the opposite of old.

practice.prompt: Look at the picture of a cat reaching near the top of the door. Which word fits?
practice.explanation: Someone with great height is tall.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.explanation: Small goes before baby: a small baby.

practice.prompt: Describe Omar. Put the describing word before 'boy'.
practice.explanation: In English, 'tall' comes before 'boy': a tall boy.

practice.prompt: Ben is twenty years old and very large. Complete the sentence.
practice.explanation: Use 'big' before 'brother': my big brother.

practice.prompt: A baby is only one year old. Complete the sentence.
practice.explanation: A baby is very young.

practice.prompt: Say this sentence aloud.
practice.explanation: Put 'short' before 'girl': a short girl.

story.hook: Who is tall and who is small in Ben's living room?

image.describe: Ben's living room: tall brother Ben stands next to short friend Leo, while baby Lily sits on the rug with Smarty.

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: Who is he, Leo?

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.text: He is Ben. Ben is my big brother.

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: Ben is a tall boy! And you, Leo?

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.text: I am a short boy, and I am young.

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.text: And look at Lily! She is our small baby sister.

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: Big brother, short brother, and a small baby!

questions.explanation: Smarty says: Ben is a tall boy!

questions.prompt: What does Leo say about himself?
questions.explanation: Leo says: I am a short boy, and I am young.

questions.prompt: Ben calls Lily our ___ baby sister.
questions.explanation: Ben says: She is our small baby sister.

mission.setup: Describe a friend or family member to Smarty using big, small, tall, short, or young.

turns.smarty: I am a small cat! Are you tall or short?
turns.hint: Say 'I am tall.' or 'I am short.'

turns.smarty: Tell me about a friend or brother or sister!
turns.hint: Say 'My brother is tall.' or 'She is a young girl.'

lessons.title: I have a pet
lessons.canDo: Say what you and others have
lessons.scenario: Mia, Tom, and Zara talk in the living room about the cat, dog, and bird they have.

items.note: Use 'I have' (and 'you/we/they have') to say what belongs to you.
Use 'has' after 'he', 'she', 'it', or one person's name.
Say 'cat' for a small furry animal that purrs, like Smarty.

image.describe: a cute black cat sitting happily on a living room rug

items.note: Say 'dog' for a friendly furry animal that wags its tail.

image.describe: a friendly brown puppy wagging its tail happily

items.note: Say 'bird' for an animal with wings and feathers.

image.describe: a cheerful little blue bird perched on a wooden stand

grammar.title: have vs. has
grammar.explanation: Use 'have' with I, you, we, and they. Use 'has' with he, she, it, or one name like Mia or Tom.

practice.prompt: Look at the picture of Smarty. Which word matches?
practice.explanation: Smarty is a cat.

practice.prompt: Look at the picture of a puppy wagging its tail. Which word fits?
practice.explanation: A puppy is a young dog.

practice.prompt: Look at the picture of an animal with wings. Which word fits?
practice.explanation: An animal with wings is a bird.

practice.prompt: Talk about yourself. Complete the sentence.
practice.explanation: Use 'I have' when talking about yourself.

practice.prompt: Tom is one boy. Complete the sentence.
practice.explanation: Use 'has' after one name like Tom.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.explanation: Zara is one girl, so we say 'Zara has'.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence about having two cats.
practice.explanation: Use 'have' with 'We' and add -s for 'two cats'.

practice.prompt: Say this sentence aloud.
practice.explanation: Use 'She has' for a girl or woman.

story.hook: Which animals do Mia, Tom, and Zara have?

image.describe: Mia's living room: Smarty the black cat sits with Mia, Tom, a friendly brown dog, and a small blue bird on a perch.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: I have a cat. His name is Smarty!

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: Yes, I am a happy cat! And Tom?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I have a big dog. He is two years old.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: Tom has a big dog, and Zara has a small bird.

lines.speaker: Zara
lines.text: Yes! My bird is small and young.

questions.explanation: Tom says: I have a big dog.
Mia says: Zara has a small bird.
Tom says: He is two years old.

mission.setup: Tell Smarty what animal or family member you have!

turns.smarty: Mia has a cat! Do you have a cat, a dog, or a bird?
turns.hint: Say 'I have a cat.' or 'I have a small dog.'

turns.smarty: Now finish this: Zara ___ a small bird.
turns.hint: Use 'has' for one person: 'Zara has a small bird.'

lessons.title: Review
lessons.scenario: Sam and Lily visit Ben's living room and talk about ages, tall and short friends, and their animals.

practice.prompt: Ben is one boy. Complete the sentence.
practice.explanation: Use 'has' with one person's name.

practice.prompt: Build the question to ask someone's age.
practice.explanation: Ask 'How old are you?' to find out someone's age.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.explanation: 'They are' goes with plural 'tall boys'.

practice.prompt: Match each sentence with the right word.
practice.explanation: Smarty is a cat, Tom has a dog, and Zara has a bird.

practice.prompt: Complete: My sister is ___ years old.
practice.explanation: Put a number like 'twenty' before 'years old'.

practice.prompt: Put the describing word before 'dog'.
practice.explanation: Adjectives like 'small' go before the noun 'dog'.

practice.prompt: Say this sentence aloud.
practice.explanation: Use 'They are' and plural 'best friends' for two or more friends.

story.hook: How many animals do Sam and Ben have in the living room?

image.describe: Ben's living room: Ben and Sam sit with two small birds and a happy dog while Smarty watches.

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: Sam and Ben, you are best friends!

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: Yes! I am twelve years old, and Ben is eleven years old.

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.text: Sam is a tall boy, and I am a short boy.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: I have a young dog, and Ben has two small birds.

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: And they have a cat friend—me!

questions.explanation: Sam says: Ben is eleven years old.
Sam says: Ben has two small birds.

mission.setup: Smarty quizzes you on ages, descriptions, and 'have/has' from Lessons 5–8.

turns.smarty: How old is a boy who is 11?
turns.hint: Say 'He is eleven years old.'

turns.smarty: Tell me something you have!
turns.hint: Say 'I have a cat.' or 'I have a sister.'

lessons.title: Meet my family
lessons.scenario: Mia's aunt, uncle, and cousin join everyone in the living room to celebrate with Smarty.

items.note: Say 'aunt' for the sister of your mother or father.

image.describe: a cheerful adult female cat wearing a floral scarf and smiling

items.note: Say 'uncle' for the brother of your mother or father.

image.describe: a tall, friendly adult male cat wearing a striped vest

items.note: Say 'cousin' for the child of your aunt and uncle.

image.describe: a playful young cat smiling and waving next to a friend

practice.prompt: Look at the picture of your mother's sister. Which word fits?
practice.explanation: Your mother or father's sister is your aunt.

practice.prompt: Look at the picture of your father's brother. Which word fits?
practice.explanation: Your mother or father's brother is your uncle.

practice.prompt: Look at the picture of your aunt and uncle's child. Which word fits?
practice.explanation: The child of your aunt and uncle is your cousin.

practice.prompt: Match each family word with its meaning.
practice.explanation: Aunt, uncle, cousin, and parents are all family members.

practice.prompt: Ben is a boy. Complete the sentence about his cousin.
practice.explanation: Ben is a boy, so use 'his'.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.audio: My uncle is tall and my aunt is short.
practice.answer: My uncle is tall and my aunt is short.
options: My uncle is tall and my aunt is short.
My cousin is eleven years old.
practice.explanation: Listen for 'uncle is tall' and 'aunt is short'.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence about Mia's cousin.
practice.answer: Her cousin has a small dog.
practice.explanation: Use 'Her' for Mia and 'has' for one cousin.

practice.prompt: Complete the sentence about your cousin's age.
practice.explanation: Add 'years old' after the number 'twelve'.

practice.prompt: Say this sentence aloud.
practice.text: This is my aunt, my uncle, and my cousin.
practice.answer: This is my aunt, my uncle, and my cousin.
practice.explanation: Introduce each family member clearly with 'my'.

story.hook: Who joins Mia's living room for the big gathering?

image.describe: Mia's bright living room filled with her aunt, uncle, cousin Leo, parents, grandparents, baby Lily, and Smarty.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: Welcome, Smarty! Meet my aunt, my uncle, and my cousin!

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: Who is she?

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: She is my aunt Zara. And he is my uncle Omar.

lines.speaker: Omar
lines.text: Hello, Smarty! This is our boy, Leo.

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.text: Hi, Mia! I am your cousin, and I am twelve years old!

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: Our parents, our grandmother, and our baby sister are here too!

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: You have a big, happy group of friends and relatives!

questions.explanation: Mia says: And he is my uncle Omar.
Leo says: Hi, Mia! I am your cousin.
Mia says: She is my aunt Zara.

mission.setup: Final challenge! Introduce your family and friends to Smarty in your own words.

turns.smarty: Introduce your aunt, uncle, or cousin!

episode.title: A Surprise in the Living Room

panels.speaker: Smarty
panels.text: Good afternoon, Mia! Good afternoon, Sam!

image.describe: Smarty the black cat waves cheerfully at the doorway of Mia and Sam's living room.

panels.speaker: Mia
panels.text: Hello, Smarty! Our parents, our aunt, and our uncle are here.

image.describe: Mia points toward her smiling parents, aunt, and uncle gathered near the living room sofa.

panels.speaker: Sam
panels.text: And this is our cousin Leo. He is twelve years old, and he is a tall boy!

image.describe: Sam introduces tall young cat Leo to Smarty.

panels.speaker: Leo
panels.text: Nice to meet you, Smarty! I have a small bird, and Mia has a young dog.

image.describe: Leo holds a perch with a small blue bird while a young brown puppy sits beside Mia.

panels.speaker: Smarty
panels.text: They are happy! And who is she?

image.describe: Smarty looks curiously at an older silver-furred cat holding a baby basket.

panels.speaker: Mia
panels.text: She is our grandmother, and she has our baby sister Lily!

image.describe: Grandmother cat smiles gently while holding a basket with tiny kitten Lily.

panels.speaker: Smarty
panels.text: Look! Grandmother has a big letter. What is it?

image.describe: Smarty stares with wide eyes at a large sealed envelope resting on the living room table.

questions.explanation: Sam says: He is twelve years old.
Leo says: I have a small bird.

questions.prompt: What does Grandmother have at the end?
questions.explanation: Smarty says: Look! Grandmother has a big letter.
